name: Kuz's Skull
summary: In the southern Barrens, Kuz's Skull marks the end of a feared Razormane raider. Kuz came from Razorfen Kraul and helped lead attacks on Horde outposts before a captive former kin sought vengeance.

sections.title: A Bitter Feud
sections.body: Kuz, Nak, and their chieftain Lok Orcbane led Razormane attacks across the southern Barrens. Sent from Razorfen Kraul, the three raiders struck travelers and settlements such as the Crossroads. Their betrayal of Mangletooth, a fellow quilboar, turned one of their own against them. They left Mangletooth to rot in a cage at Camp Taurajo. From that cage, he revealed Kuz's location to Horde champions willing to kill the raider and take her head.

sections.title: Proof of Retribution
sections.body: Kuz's Skull proves to Mangletooth that one of the three leaders of the southern warband is dead. For him, the head brings satisfaction against the tribe that abandoned him. Across the Barrens, Kuz's death breaks the command behind the Razormane attacks and gives the supply roads across the plains a brief respite.

faq.answer: Kuz was one of three Razormane quilboar sent from Razorfen Kraul into the southern Barrens. With Nak and Lok Orcbane, she directed ambushes and raids against Horde encampments and supply lines.

faq.q: Why does Mangletooth want Kuz's skull?
faq.answer: Mangletooth wants Kuz's skull because Kuz and the other Razormane left him to die in a cage at Camp Taurajo. Seeking vengeance before his own death, he points Horde champions toward his rivals and asks for their skulls as proof.

faq.q: Where is Kuz found in the Barrens?
faq.answer: Kuz is found in the southern Barrens, with the Razormane quilboar south of Camp Taurajo near the thorny border regions.

faq.q: What happens after Kuz is slain?
faq.answer: When Kuz's Skull and the heads of Nak and Lok Orcbane reach Mangletooth, they break the leadership behind the Razormane attacks and help secure the southern trade routes.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, taking Kuz's head helps protect settlements such as the Crossroads and Camp Taurajo from organized quilboar attacks.
